title: You’re Wasting HOURS in RuneScape Dragonwilds 1.0
author: BiggySweats
chapters: Stop Farming Rats for Coarse Thread
Fishing Is Better Than You Think
What Did You Learn Too Late?
description:
RuneScape Dragonwilds 1.0 has a load of systems that can quietly waste hours or make the game much harder if you don’t realise how they actually work.

This guide covers some of the biggest things Dragonwilds barely explains, including Lodestone Law Rune costs, Sanguine Urns, the Construction 40 Personal Chest, Storage Ledger, respawning Vault Cores, Masterwork and Vestige weapon Ascension, Coarse Thread, Fishing and Agility carry-weight upgrades.

If you’ve been burning through Law Runes, constantly travelling back to base, binning old weapons or doing certain grinds the slow way, these are the things worth knowing.

transcript.text: Runescape Dragon Wilds has quite a few things that it just does not explain very well. And I'm obviously not talking
about the usual beginner tips like build a bed, cook your food, upgrade your tools. I mean stuff that can genuinely
save you hours. Your load stone can literally charge you more law runes depending on what you're carrying. Those
sanguin earns you polywar past. They're not just some random collectible. Every unique one gives you 10 permanent max
HP. And there are weapons you might have already thrown into a chest or completely replace that you can actually
keep upgrading later. So, I've gone through the current version of Dragon Wilds, and these are the things I
genuinely think are worth knowing because some of them can completely change how you approach the game. And
trust me, the first one has probably already cost you a ton of law runes. Load stones. I know traveling further
costs more law runes. That makes entire sense. What isn't nearly as obvious is how much weight you're carrying is also
part of the cost. So if you finish farming, you're massively overweight, your inventory is rammed, and then you
teleport all the way back across Ashenfall, you're basically paying extra for the privilege of carrying all of
that crap home. Jagex actually gave an example where a player carrying 388 weight traveling a long distance played
58 lore runes. That changes the way I look at load stones completely. Before you teleport, look at what you're
carrying. Do you actually need all of it? Can some of it go somewhere else first? And once you unlock home
teleport, you've also got another option. Home teleport sends you directly to your claim bed for 15 l runes.
Although it does have a long cool down. So don't just mindlessly click the nearest load stone every single time
your bags are full because over an entire playthrough you're potentially just wasting away tons of law runes. And
this is the one I think is really easy to underestimate. Sanguin Earns. If you found one of these while exploring and
thought, "These are cool. I'll come back later for all the collectible stuff." No, you got to use them now. Every
unique sanguin earned permanently increases your maximum HP by 10. Not temporarily, not while you're wearing
something, 10 permanent health. So, if you're pushing into the harder regions and you're wondering why you're getting
absolutely slapped, gear obviously matters, but there's also a permanent character power sitting around the world
that you can just completely miss. This is one of those things where I wouldn't go and follow a map and ruin the entire
exploration side of the game for yourself. But when you do find one, absolutely do not ignore it. Now, this
is probably one of my favorites. At construction 40, you unlock the personal chest spell. And the name does not sell
this thing whatsoever because this lets you access your personal storage from basically anywhere in the world. So,
think about how much time you spend exploring, filling your inventory, getting overweight, and then going right
back to base we go again. And the way I'd use this is for the stuff you don't need every second. Keep your actual
essentials on you. Then use the personal chest for the heavy materials and backup
stuff you'd normally have to run all the way home for. That's where this becomes probably useful. You can effectively
carry your own remote storage access with you. And people are still discovering this ridiculously late.
There are people with tens of hours into the game finding out what this thing actually does. The cast cost 20 l runes
and 50 astral runes. So obviously don't spam it every 8 seconds like some maniac. So construction isn't just about
ooh nice, I can build a few new things. It becomes I can fundamentally change how long I stay out exploring before I
need to go home. If you're somebody who normally ignores building skills because you don't care about making a giga
mansion, construction 40 is still worth knowing about. Then you've got the storage ledger. And if you've built one
but haven't properly used it, please do. Normally you can come back from the expedition looking like you've robbed
the entire continent. Logs ore random food materials. Absolute crap everywhere. Then you run around your
storage room opening chest after chest trying to remember where everything goes. With the storage ledger, you
interact with it and items in your inventory that already have a matching stack inside a linked chest can be
automatically sorted into the correct storage. That's it. You come home, ledger done. And this is what I mean by
things the game has that don't sound particularly exciting until you realize how much repeated crap they remove.
Personal chest help while you're away, but storage ledger helps the second you get home. Those two alone make inventory
management much less annoying. This one is important because the game makes vault cores feel way more precious than
they actually are. When you start opening vaults and getting cores, it's very easy to think, I probably shouldn't
waste these. There must only be so many. And it does really feel like that, especially because load stones are so
useful. But completed vaults can be revisited, and the vault cores respawn after a few in-game days. So, you can
farm the same vault again and again. That means you don't need to be scared of actually building out your load stone
network because you think you're going to permanently run out of your cores. And I'd much rather know this early than
spend half the game doing the classic RPG thing where you save every resource for later and then you finish the game
with 900 of them sitting in your storage. People are still asking whether vault cause respawn, which tells you how
easy it is to assume these things are one and done. And if even one of these has already saved you from wasting a
load of time, join the sweats, hit the sub button, like, comment, because I've got loads more Dragon Wild stuff coming.
And if you want 10% off gamer subs, use the code biggie at checkout. Sadly, it does not reduce your load stone costs. I
did check. It would have been nice. Now, gear progression can trick you a little bit. You move into a new region. You
unlock the next power level. Your old weapons number looks worse. Easy decision, right? chuck it in the
storage, make the new thing, and never look at it again. Except some of your good weapons can actually stay relevant.
The Mystic Forge has ascension cores, and those can be used to upgrade masterwork and vestage weapons into
higher tiers. So, if you've got a unique weapon or something you really like using, don't automatically assume lower
power level, therefore useless forever. Check whether it's something that can actually be ascended first, because
there are some weapons you might replace purely because the number looks old, when the entire point is that you can
bring them forward with you. And just to be clear, I'm specifically talking about the documented Masterwork and vestage
weapon system here. I'm not telling you every random bit of gear you can pick up can magically become endgame bis. Don't
go blaming me when your wooden club doesn't become Excalibur. And this one is much smaller than permanent HP or
remote storage, but holy crap can it save you from doing something incredibly boring. Coarse thread. Early on, it's
very easy to end up getting the materials for this through animals and assume that's just what you're supposed
to keep doing. But once you've got access to the spinning wheel, flax can be turned into coarse thread. Flax, the
blue plants you've probably been running past about 600 times throughout your journey. So instead of going out
murdering the local rat population every time you need more thread, grab the flax
and spin it. It's such a tiny thing, but this is exactly the kind of tiny thing where if nobody tells you, you can spend
an embarrassing amount of time doing something the slow way because you assume that's how the game works. And
Dragon Wilds has loads of stuff like this. If you've basically been ignoring fishing because you think it's just
another survival game food skill, well, don't because fishing is actually tied to some of the best healing you can
carry around in the game. Jagex specifically reworked healing so that food became much more important. And
fish are supposed to be the best option when what you care about is getting a big chunk of that health back quickly.
And that's something I think it's really easy to miss. You can look at fishing and think, "Well, it's just some fish."
Meanwhile, you're pushing harder areas, taking massive damage, and relying on whatever random food you've already got
sitting in a chest. High-end fish can heal a ridiculous amount. And more importantly, Jagex describes fishing as
giving you the best healing per stack. So, if combat is starting to hit harder and you're wondering why your healing
feels awful, it might not be your armor. You might have just completely ignored one of the games actual healing
progression systems. And one last thing, because this actually connects back to what I said right at the start about
carry weight. Agility is way more useful than I originally gave it credit for, because at level 50 and again at level
75, you unlock permanent increases to maximum carry weight. So, agility isn't just, oh, I can move a little bit
faster. is literally a part of your inventory progression as well. You can stay out gathering longer. You can carry
more before becoming overloaded. And because we've already established that weight affects how expensive load stone
travel can become, the extra capacity actually matters. When you first look at agility, it's exactly the kind of skill
that you just think about passively leveling without realizing it's quietly making one of those most annoying parts
of the game less painful. So yes, don't look at agility just as movement. It's doing more for you than that. So I want
to know one thing from you. What is something in Dragon Wilds that you found way later than you should have? Because
if there's something properly good that I've missed, chuck it in the comments. I genuinely want to see what else people
have found. If you enjoyed the video, hit the like button, subscribe, and join the sweats. You've also got YouTube
membership and Patreon if you want to support the channel directly. I'm live over on Twitch all week playing the new
Silent Hill on Thursday with all my socials linked below. Come and follow. I'll catch you in the next one. Peace.

comments.author: @jlayman89
comments.text:
Few bonus tips.
1. Keep the materials for a lodgestone or two in the personal chest. If you find a good spot, you can open this and drop one. Or if you want to keep going but need storage space, use it as a "save point" to lodgestone home, deposit, then return to the same spot. You can break it and get the materials back when you return. 
2. If you're super overweight, as in you mined a ton and you have like 4+ tons, drop it all in the chest and then lodgestone home, less overall runes. Or use it to dump excess in to treat it like extended storage. 
3. Put a lodgestone outside all vaults. Even after the 2nd round of going around to get more, youre even. Even if you only get rhe boss one, but if you run backward a bit normally you can get 2 fast. Now you have a cycle to get as many as you want. 

Last tip is one i learned too late, use multiple styles. At minimum 2. For example, there's no penalty for using magic in melee armor, you just wont get the set bonuses. You honestly should use all 3, theyre all good in different situations. I even go as far as to have a 2h and 1h+shield for all 3 for 6 setups. I cannot stress enough how much this helps. If you're strictly a magic user and find you get cornered a mobbed too often, toss in a melee setup with a 1h+shield. Now ehen enemies get in close, you can swap to this instead and its significantly easier to get out and fight. Trying to run and kite and shoot them can take ages when they're fast. If you just whip out the melee setup after you pick off a few, then melee the remainder, its way faster AND safer. Also, as you get further, enemy weaknesses matter more, ao always having the ability to find it is huge. 

Bonus, mixing and matching armor sets is the way to go. 1 magic piece allows you step back and regen stamina way faster so you can get back into it, even if you're only using melee and ranged. There's plenty of combos that work great. I tend toward 2 melee or magic and 1 of the other. Bith are good depending on what im doing.

comments.author: @richlewis6800
comments.text: So on law runes ! In the start , when you have to find them , it is ok to try to save them . But later on , after you hit 50 rune crafting and can make them . They give the most exp per rune crafted and this becomes very important once you hit 94+ rune crafting looking to max it to 99 . On fishing , I hate it lol .It took me 10 hours to go from level 1-99 in agility . It  took me 18.5 hours to go from 98-99 in fishing . The food seems good , but it cancels all other food buffs . If your playing the game right , with efficiency in mind . Then your going to have a 10% exp gain food buff equipped at all times . Fish buffs give you nothing worth having , ever ! There are some later on like belt fish that make good supplemental healing that will not cancel your other buffs in a boss fight . But that is it really . For the time it takes , it is a horrible addition to the game at the moment . Now , I was 90 + in everything when it was introduced , so maybe early on it is good , I can not say . But in late game , it is awful . I mention these things because you do not want to get used to sparing law runes and relying on fishing as this will change mid game and start to hurt your progression . On a side note , save ALL the trout you get early on in the starting area . You will need hundreds of fishing pots later on , trust me lol . You want to hold on to them till you can make the big ones that give 30% exp for 600 seconds . This is late game but you will thank me later =) . Fishing is by far the hardest skill to master , it takes forever to max it out . If you care about maxing that is . You will want the ring 5% exp , the food buff 10% exp and that potion 30% exp gain and it still takes forever to level it .
